Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 105, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾: that is, has it not reached your knowledge what your Lord did to the companions of the elephant.

The companions of the elephant: that is, Mahmud, which was the largest of them, and with him twelve elephants; its owner was Abraha.

﴿Did He not make their plot into misguidance?﴾: that is, in the destruction of the Ka'bah.

Misguidance (tadlil): that is, in loss and destruction.

Ababil: that is, in flocks, flock after flock.

Sijjil: that is, baked clay.

Like eaten straw (ka'asf ma'kul): that is, like the leaves of a crop eaten by beasts and trampled under their feet.

The meaning of the verses:

The Exalted's saying ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ up to ﴿eaten﴾ are five verses which contain an account of a great event that took place around the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ). Its summary is that Abraha al-Ashram, the governor of Yemen on behalf of the king of Abyssinia, decided to build a house in Sana'a, Yemen, calling the Arabs to pilgrimage to it instead of their pilgrimage to the Sacred House, with the aim of diverting trade and profits from Makkah to Yemen. He presented this to the Abyssinian king, who agreed and was pleased with it. When he built the house, "the church," and named it al-Qulleys, no like of it had been built in its history, a man from Quraysh came and defecated in it and smeared its walls with filth, out of spite. He left. When Abraha al-Ashram saw it in that state, he flared with rage and equipped an army to raid Makkah and destroy the Ka'bah. With him were thirteen elephants, among them an elephant called Mahmud, which was the largest of them. They advanced, and no tribe of the Arabs that stood in their way was spared, for they fought and defeated it, until they reached near Makkah. An embassy took place between them and the sheikh of Makkah, Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, grandfather of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the negotiations ended with Abraha returning Abd al-Muttalib's camels, and then he could do as he wished with the Ka'bah. The men of Makkah were ordered to empty the city and take refuge at the mountaintops with their women and children, fearing the harm that the invading and oppressive army might inflict on them. Then Abraha's army moved and reached the valley of Muhassir, and while it was proceeding through the middle of the valley, behold, flocks of birds, one flock after another, were sent against that army, carrying stones, each stone the size between a chickpea and a lentil. No stone fell on a man without melting him and scattering his flesh, so they perished, and Abraha fled with his flesh scattering, and died on the road. This was a victory from God for the inhabitants of His sanctuary and the guardians of His House, and from then on the Arabs continued to honor the Ka'bah, the Sacred Precinct and its inhabitants until today.

The Exalted's saying ﴿Have you not considered how﴾ addresses His Messenger, reminding him of His mighty act in destroying the tyrants. Where is the strength of the oppressors of Quraysh, such as al-'As ibn Wa'il, 'Amr ibn Hisham, al-Walid and 'Uqbah, compared with the strength of Abraha? God destroyed Abraha's forces in an hour. So be patient, O Muhammad, and do not burden yourself with worry over these enemies, for they have an appointed time. The surah is thus a reminder for admonition and reflection.

This is the explanation of the verses: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ That is, has it not reached your knowledge what your Lord did to the companions of the elephant.

﴿Did He not make their plot into misguidance?﴾ That is, did He not make what they plotted against our House and our Sanctuary into loss and error, so that they gained nothing but disgrace and ruin? ﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks﴾ That is, flock after flock, which were seen emerging from the sea by the men of Makkah who had taken refuge at the mountaintops, as they passed over them carrying stones of sijjil. Each bird carried three stones, like a chickpea and a lentil: one in its beak and two in its talons, each in one talon, which it hurled at them, so that their flesh was torn to pieces and scattered, and He made them ﴿like eaten straw﴾, that is, like a field of crops into which livestock entered and ate its stalks, that is its leaves, and broke its stems and crushed it. So it was one of the signs of God.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Consolation of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for the oppression he encounters from the disbelievers of Quraysh.

2- Reminding Quraysh of the act of God, the Mighty and Majestic, as a warning and a deterrent to them.

3- Manifestations of God's power in His management of His creation and His seizing of His enemies.
